sector_model: equity REIT (industrial, six coastal U.S. markets); use FFO (self-computed NAREIT style because the 10-Q does not give FFO), same-store NOI, occupancy, lease rollover, net debt to EBITDA; GAAP net income distorted by gains on sales; generic FCF and P/E not used
thesis: Terreno owns 317 industrial buildings (20.5M sq ft) plus improved land in coastal gateway markets, 97.8% leased for buildings with 687 tenants (largest 6.8% of rent). Q3 2026 same-store NOI rose 4.7% (6.5% for nine months) and cash rents on new and renewed leases were 27.7% higher than prior rents. Net debt is 805M, 2.2x adjusted EBITDA, with interest coverage 10.3x and 11.1% debt to market capitalization. At 66.41 (2026-11-06) and about 110.3M shares the equity is worth 7.33B; self-computed Q3 FFO of 78.9M (0.72 per diluted share, 2.88 annualized) gives about 23x annualized FFO and a 3.4% dividend yield (2.28 annualized, about 79% of that FFO).
counterthesis: A 23x FFO multiple and a roughly 4.7% annualized NOI yield on enterprise value is not cheap, and management is selling stock at about 66 to fund growth (6.03M shares, 393M net proceeds in nine months; shares up 6.0% since December), so per-share growth depends on acquisitions earning more than the cost of equity. Weighted average remaining lease term is only 4.1 years (3.5 in New York/New Jersey, 3.2 in San Francisco and 2.7 in Seattle), so rents reset quickly if market rents soften; the 27.7% cash rent gains reflect leases signed years ago and may not repeat. Improved land is 9.4% of rent at only 95.5% leased. 44.6% of debt is floating and 150M of debt matures in 2027 and 273M in 2028. GAAP net income fell 20% in nine months only because 2025 included larger gains on sales (128.9M vs 59.0M). FFO is my own calculation (net income less gains plus all depreciation and amortization), not a company-reported or AFFO figure; recurring capex, straight-line rents and lease-intangible amortization are not removed. The 10-K, rent roll expirations by year, NAV or cap-rate comparison and peer multiples were not read.
invalidation: Same-store NOI growth turning negative or occupancy below 95%; cash rent change on rollovers falling below 10%; net debt to adjusted EBITDA above 4.5x (management's own limit); ATM issuance continuing while the stock trades near or below estimated NAV; coastal market rents declining for two quarters.
